paragraphs: This paper studies whether music fans can collectively increase an underrepresented artist’s visibility by changing playlists they already control. The intervention is specific: insert one of the artist’s songs at a strategically chosen position. The researchers introduce two simple placement strategies for influencing a transformer-based recommender trained on those playlists.

The strategies use statistical properties of the recommendation model, including abrupt changes in which songs get recommended and the uneven distribution of song popularity. This makes placement an additional source of influence beyond merely adding more occurrences of a song. The experiments use a publicly released recommendation model from a major streaming platform.

In the reported evaluation, groups controlling less than 0.01% of the training data could obtain up to 40 times as many recommendations, on average, as songs with similar training frequencies. Recommendations for other songs were largely preserved, and gains extended across different artists. These findings suggest that carefully coordinated participation can influence recommendations without necessarily functioning as an adversarial intervention.
neurips-2024-algorithmic-collective-acti.tldr: Small groups of fans can strategically position songs in playlists to substantially increase recommendations while largely preserving recommendations for other songs.

paragraphs: Allocation problems require an agent to divide limited resources among several recipients repeatedly. Examples include distributing investment funds or assigning computing workloads to servers. These decisions often face linear constraints that must hold at every step, such as a cap on investment in one sector. Finding useful decisions inside the resulting restricted action space is a central learning challenge.

The paper proposes generating an allocation sequentially, sampling the amount assigned to one entity before moving to the next. This autoregressive approach makes the allocation a series of connected choices. The authors also introduce a de-biasing mechanism because sequential sampling creates an initial bias that the learning procedure needs to counter.

The method is evaluated on portfolio optimization, computational workload distribution, and a synthetic allocation task. Across these evaluations, the authors report better performance than a range of constrained reinforcement learning methods. The contribution combines a structured way to generate resource allocations with a correction for the bias introduced by that structure, addressing both decision construction and learning behavior.
neurips-2024-autoregressive-policy-optim.tldr: Sequential allocation sampling and a dedicated de-biasing mechanism improve performance on three resource-allocation tasks with strict linear constraints.

paragraphs: Diffusion policies learn behavior from demonstrations using models that can represent several plausible actions. Their growing use raises a safety question: how reliably do they act when their inputs are deliberately manipulated? The paper argues that attacks developed for earlier policy networks are ineffective against the chained computation and injected randomness of diffusion policies.

To investigate this vulnerability, the authors introduce DP-Attacker, a collection of attack algorithms designed for diffusion-based control. The study covers offline and online attacks, as well as modifications spread across an input or confined to a patch. These scenarios examine vulnerabilities under several distinct ways of presenting adversarial information to a policy.

Experiments attack pretrained diffusion policies on multiple manipulation tasks and report substantial reductions in task success across all studied scenarios. Offline attacks produce transferable perturbations usable across frames, and physical patches placed in the environment also deceive the model. The findings show that the architectural features complicating previous attacks do not, by themselves, establish resistance to attacks designed specifically for diffusion policies.
neurips-2024-diffusion-policy-attacker-c.tldr: DP-Attacker exposes vulnerabilities in diffusion policies through several attack settings, including transferable perturbations and physical patches.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation creates a small synthetic training set intended to stand in for a much larger original dataset. Its value depends on how much useful information the synthetic examples retain. This paper focuses on redundancy: if many synthesized examples contain similar features, a compact dataset can spend its limited capacity repeatedly representing the same information.

The authors analyze synthetic-data diversity theoretically and empirically, focusing on a synthesis approach whose separate operations can run in parallel. They propose dynamic, directed adjustments to the weights governing synthesis. These adjustments guide each synthetic instance toward being both representative and distinct, while making each batch reflect a large and changing subset of the original data.

Experiments on CIFAR, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K report superior performance with low computational expense. The stated findings support diversity as a useful design objective for this synthesis setting. The method’s significance is that it connects efficient parallel generation with broader coverage of the original dataset, giving the small synthetic collection more varied information to carry into training.
neurips-2024-diversity-driven-synthesis-.tldr: Dynamic, directed weight adjustments make distilled datasets more diverse and representative, improving reported performance with low computational expense.

paragraphs: A forecasting system may need to predict different distances into the future depending on the request. ElasTST addresses this changing forecast horizon within one time-series transformer. A central design goal is consistency: extending or shortening the requested horizon should leave predictions for the shared future positions unchanged.

The model produces future outputs non-autoregressively, using placeholders and structured attention masks to enforce that invariance. It also uses tunable rotary position embeddings to capture periods relevant to time series. A multi-scale patch design combines detailed local information with coarser patterns, giving the model access to temporal structure at different resolutions.

During training, horizon reweighting approximates the effect of randomly sampling several forecast lengths while using a single fixed horizon setting. This connects the training procedure to the varied requests expected at inference. Experiments compare ElasTST with leading time-series architectures and contemporary foundation models and support the effectiveness of its design components. The reported result is a model built specifically for robust forecasting when users change how far ahead they want predictions.
neurips-2024-elastst-towards-robust-vari.tldr: ElasTST combines horizon-consistent attention, adaptable temporal encoding, and multi-scale inputs to support forecasts of varying lengths.

paragraphs: Dataset condensation aims to replace a large training collection with a compact synthetic one that retains useful training performance. Applying it to object detection is difficult because a detector must learn both what objects are and where they appear. Detection datasets also contain large, high-resolution images, making them challenging for existing condensation methods.

DCOD separates the process into Fetch and Forge stages. Fetch stores important classification and localization information in model parameters. Forge then reconstructs synthetic images through model inversion, using that stored information. To handle several objects within an image, the method separates foreground and background processing and adds an incremental patch-expansion mechanism to increase foreground diversity.

The authors report strong results across detection datasets and shorter detector training times. At a reported compression rate of 1%, DCOD achieves AP50 values of 46.4% on VOC and 24.7% on COCO. These findings show that a very compact synthetic dataset can retain useful information for both components of detection, extending condensation beyond the image-classification setting where it has mainly been studied.
neurips-2024-fetch-and-forge-efficient-d.tldr: DCOD condenses object-detection data by storing task information in a model and reconstructing compact synthetic training images.

paragraphs: Triplane Gaussian Splatting, or TGS, can generate a 3D model from a single image within seconds. This paper considers how image owners might protect their work against unauthorized use in that reconstruction process. The proposed protection modifies an image before it is supplied to TGS, embedding perturbations described as invisible in the source image.

These geometry cloaks carry a customized message designed to appear in the generated reconstruction. Their objective is more specific than reducing output quality: they steer the reconstruction toward an identifiable pattern that functions as a watermark. The same intervention therefore disrupts the intended reconstruction and embeds an ownership-related signal in the resulting output.

The authors report that extensive experiments verify the effectiveness of this approach. Its contribution is a targeted form of image protection tied to how TGS converts images into geometry. The stated result concerns making attempted reconstructions reveal a recognizable message, providing copyright holders with a way to associate those outputs with their protected images.
neurips-2024-geometry-cloak-preventing-t.tldr: Geometry cloaks invisibly modify images so that TGS reconstructions reveal a customized watermark instead of the intended geometry.

paragraphs: This paper investigates how a trained transformer uses multiple attention heads when learning sparse linear regression from examples in its context. Earlier theoretical work showed that particular transformer parameter settings can implement gradient descent. Here, the emphasis is on understanding the mechanisms that appear after training, rather than only establishing what a transformer can express.

Experiments reveal a difference between layers: several heads are used and are essential in the first layer, while later layers usually need only one. The authors explain this pattern with a two-stage algorithm. The first layer preprocesses the contextual examples, and subsequent layers perform relatively simple optimization steps on the resulting representation.

The paper also demonstrates that this preprocess-then-optimize procedure can substantially outperform naive gradient descent and ridge regression. Additional experiments support the proposed explanation. The findings give multiple heads a concrete role in the studied setting: they help construct the information on which later optimization operates. This provides a more differentiated account of in-context learning than treating every layer as another identical optimization step.
neurips-2024-how-transformers-utilize-mu.tldr: In sparse linear regression, trained transformers use multiple early attention heads to preprocess examples before later layers perform simpler optimization.

paragraphs: Vision-and-language navigation asks an embodied agent to move through an environment by following human instructions. This paper extends that task to environments containing dynamic human activity. It addresses the reliance of existing frameworks on static surroundings and optimal expert supervision, assumptions that restrict their relevance to navigation around people.

The authors introduce the HA3D simulator, which adds human activities to Matterport3D, and the HA-R2R dataset, which augments Room-to-Room navigation data with descriptions of those activities. They also present two agents: an expert-supervised cross-modal model and a decision-transformer model trained with non-expert supervision. Together, these provide ways to study different training strategies in the expanded setting.

Evaluation incorporates measures that account for human activity and analyzes the challenges introduced by HA-VLN. The findings emphasize that further work is needed for reliable adaptation and robustness in real-world human environments. The main contribution is therefore a task, simulator, dataset, and set of agents that make these challenges available for systematic study and future simulation-to-reality research.
neurips-2024-human-aware-vision-and-lang.tldr: HA-VLN introduces navigation benchmarks and agents that account for dynamic human activity and different levels of expert supervision.

paragraphs: Language models trained on short sequences can struggle with much longer inputs because those inputs differ from training and contain distracting information. A common response is additional training on longer sequences, which requires substantial computation and can change model capabilities. InfLLM instead investigates how far existing models can go through a different way of accessing context.

The method stores distant context in additional memory units. When processing a token, it retrieves relevant units for attention computation, allowing a limited active context window to draw on information from much earlier in the sequence. This memory-and-retrieval mechanism is introduced without fine-tuning the underlying language model.

The authors report that models pretrained on only a few thousand tokens achieve performance comparable to competitive baselines that receive continued long-sequence training. They also report effective capture of long-distance dependencies at a sequence length of 1,024K. The findings support context-memory management as a way to expose long-input capabilities already present in pretrained models, without requiring additional parameter training.
neurips-2024-infllm-training-free-long-c.tldr: InfLLM retrieves relevant distant context from memory to extend language-model context handling without additional training.

paragraphs: Studying emergence in a time series requires choosing variables that describe the system at a larger scale. That choice is difficult when the relevant collective patterns are not known beforehand. Although information-theoretic measures can quantify emergence, researchers still need a way to find the representations to which those measures should be applied.

The paper combines representation learning with differentiable information estimators to discover emergent variables directly from data. This links the search for a useful representation to quantitative information about emergence. The authors also extend the method to learn several independent features, allowing it to extract a varied collection of emergent quantities rather than a single representation.

On synthetic data, the method identifies emergent variables and recovers the known emergence values. A modified version also scales to experimental recordings of primate brain activity. These results establish a route from controlled validation to biological data analysis. The broader prospect is to use learned variables to investigate emergent cognitive structure in biological and artificial systems.
neurips-2024-learning-diverse-causally-e.tldr: The method learns diverse emergent variables from time series and is demonstrated on synthetic data and primate brain recordings.

paragraphs: LoD-Loc estimates a drone’s position and orientation using a Level-of-Detail 3D map. Its central idea is to compare geometric outlines: a wireframe projected from the map is aligned with a wireframe predicted from the camera image by a neural network. This allows localization without relying on a complex textured representation of the scene.

The method starts with a coarse pose supplied by the drone’s sensor. It hierarchically evaluates uniformly sampled candidate poses, assigning costs according to how well their projected lines align with the predicted image wireframe. The resulting cost volume represents pose probabilities. After choosing the most probable pose, a differentiable optimization procedure refines all six position-and-orientation degrees of freedom.

The researchers collect two datasets with LoD3.0 and LoD2.0 maps, real RGB images, and reference poses because no public dataset covered this problem. Their benchmark results show strong localization performance, including improvements over leading methods using textured 3D models. The findings support geometric line alignment as an effective basis for aerial localization given a coarse starting pose.
neurips-2024-lod-loc-aerial-visual-local.tldr: LoD-Loc refines a drone’s coarse pose by aligning image-predicted wireframes with projections from a simplified 3D map.

paragraphs: Prompt-based continual learning adapts pretrained models with relatively few learned parameters and can reduce forgetting without a memory buffer. This paper seeks a theoretical explanation for why prompting works well in that setting. Its analysis connects attention inside pretrained models, including vision transformers, to a particular mixture-of-experts architecture.

In that interpretation, the attention block contains linear experts and gating scores with a quadratic form. Prefix tuning can then be understood as adding new experts associated with particular tasks. This perspective makes the gating mechanism a concrete design target: it governs how the added experts contribute to the model’s computation.

The authors use this insight to propose Non-linear Residual Gates, or NoRGa. The mechanism combines nonlinear activation with a residual connection to improve continual learning while keeping the method parameter efficient. The paper supports its effectiveness theoretically and through experiments across multiple benchmarks and pretraining approaches. Its contribution is both an explanation of prompt adaptation and a practical architectural change derived from that explanation.
neurips-2024-mixture-of-experts-meets-pr.tldr: A mixture-of-experts interpretation of attention motivates NoRGa, a parameter-efficient gating mechanism that improves prompt-based continual learning.

paragraphs: MR-Ben evaluates whether language models can inspect reasoning and identify where it goes wrong. The motivation is that benchmarks focused on final answers are beginning to saturate, making further progress harder to distinguish. The proposed task shifts attention to the reasoning process by asking models to locate and analyze possible errors in automatically generated solution steps.

The benchmark contains 5,975 questions curated by human experts across subjects including physics, chemistry, logic, and coding. Its meta-reasoning tasks require checking assumptions, conditions, calculations, and logical connections. This is intended to assess the careful examination associated with system-2 thinking, including the ability to scrutinize a proposed solution.

Using dedicated evaluation metrics, the authors identify weaknesses in both open-source and closed-source models. OpenAI’s o1 series performs strongly through scrutiny of the solution space, while many other leading models fall substantially behind. The results suggest potential shortcomings in those models’ training or inference approaches and show how process-focused evaluation can distinguish capabilities that outcome-based benchmarks may capture less effectively.
neurips-2024-mr-ben-a-meta-reasoning-ben.tldr: MR-Ben tests whether language models can find and analyze reasoning errors, revealing substantial differences between leading models.

paragraphs: Many approaches to reinforcement learning from human feedback evaluate preferences at the level of a single response. This paper addresses interactions where success depends on a whole conversation, including planning across turns toward a longer-term goal. Its training signal compares two complete conversations, allowing preferences to concern the interaction as a whole.

For the tabular setting, the authors develop a policy-optimization algorithm based on mirror descent and prove convergence to a Nash equilibrium. This provides a theoretical result for their general multi-turn preference problem. They also develop a deep reinforcement learning version for evaluating the approach beyond that tabular formulation.

The experimental setting includes Education Dialogue, a new environment where a teacher agent helps a student learn a randomly chosen topic. The deep variant outperforms RLHF baselines there. In another environment with explicit rewards, the preference-based algorithm matches a reward-based reinforcement learning baseline despite receiving only the weaker preference signal. Together, the results support learning from whole-interaction comparisons when progress depends on multiple connected decisions.
neurips-2024-multi-turn-reinforcement-le.tldr: Learning from preferences over complete conversations improves multi-turn behavior, with a convergence guarantee in the tabular setting.

paragraphs: Physical surrogate models predict how a system changes across space and time. Multiple physics pretraining, or MPP, trains one transformer backbone on several heterogeneous physical systems together. The goal is to learn features useful across systems, providing a starting point that can transfer to new prediction tasks.

MPP uses autoregressive prediction and a shared embedding and normalization strategy. This projects the fields from different systems into a common representation, enabling them to contribute to the same training process. The approach is evaluated on a broad benchmark oriented toward fluid mechanics, covering both the systems used during pretraining and downstream tasks.

A single pretrained transformer matches or exceeds task-specific baselines on every pretraining subtask without fine-tuning. For downstream systems with previously unseen physical components or higher dimensionality, fine-tuned MPP models make more accurate multi-step predictions than models trained from scratch or adapted from video foundation models. These findings support learning across several physical systems as a useful basis for both shared prediction and later specialization.
neurips-2024-multiple-physics-pretrainin.tldr: Pretraining a transformer across multiple physical systems improves shared prediction and transfer to new physical forecasting tasks.

paragraphs: Sketch re-identification retrieves a person’s photograph from a gallery using a sketch. The central difficulty is matching information across two very different visual forms, especially when sketches omit detail. OLTM uses automatically obtained textual information to help connect the sketch and image representations without requiring additional annotations.

A pretrained visual question-answering model first extracts multiple attributes of the target. A text-prompt reasoning module then combines learnable prompts with optimal transport to produce informative global and local text representations. These representations guide alignment at both coarse and fine levels, giving the two visual modalities a shared semantic reference.

The paper also introduces a triplet assignment loss that uses the overall data distribution when shaping distances within and between identity classes. This expands the training signal beyond the distance between two individual samples. Experiments on two public benchmarks report consistent robustness and improvements over leading methods. The contribution combines automatically generated attribute guidance, multi-scale textual alignment, and a distribution-aware training objective for retrieving identities across sketches and photographs.
neurips-2024-optimal-transport-based-lab.tldr: OLTM uses automatically extracted attributes and optimal-transport-based text representations to improve sketch-to-photo person retrieval without extra annotations.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a physical object from one image involves more than reproducing its visible shape. The paper describes that shape as the result of mechanical properties, external forces, and the object’s rest geometry. Methods that assume rigidity or ignore forces can produce reconstructions that deform undesirably or become unstable when subjected to physical conditions.

The proposed optimization framework represents those three attributes explicitly and connects them through static equilibrium. Equilibrium is imposed as a hard constraint during reconstruction, making physical compatibility part of the shape-generation process. The framework therefore seeks a physical configuration whose behavior agrees with the intended appearance shown in the image.

Evaluations on a dataset collected from Objaverse show consistent improvements in physical realism over existing methods. The authors also identify dynamic simulation and 3D printing as practical applications, where the interaction between shape and forces matters directly. The main contribution is a reconstruction formulation that incorporates material behavior and loading conditions into the search for a physically compatible object.
neurips-2024-physically-compatible-3d-ob.tldr: The framework reconstructs objects from single images while enforcing static equilibrium between geometry, mechanical properties, and external forces.

paragraphs: This paper reviews a competition designed to make models of mouse vision directly comparable. Predicting neuronal responses to moving visual input is difficult because the relationship between what an animal sees and how its neurons respond is nonlinear. The benchmark provides a common dataset and evaluation procedure for testing neural-network models of that relationship.

The dataset contains recordings from 78,853 neurons in the primary visual cortex of ten mice, with two hours of dynamic stimuli per neuron. It also includes behavioral measurements such as running speed, pupil dilation, and eye movements. Separate competition tracks evaluate predictions for natural stimuli within the training domain and for out-of-distribution stimuli, making generalization an explicit part of the comparison.

The competition attracted more than 160 submissions from 22 teams and produced several new model architectures. Winning teams improved on the previous state-of-the-art model by a reported 50%. The continuing availability of the data and evaluation infrastructure makes this contribution a shared foundation for comparing future models of visual responses to dynamic input.
neurips-2024-retrospective-for-the-dynam.tldr: The Dynamic Sensorium competition established a large shared benchmark for predicting mouse visual-cortex activity and spurred substantial model improvements.

paragraphs: Metagenomic binning groups DNA fragments from a biological sample to help determine which microbes are present. Its effectiveness depends on representations that make relevant similarities between fragments accessible to a clustering method. This paper revisits k-mer composition as the basis for those representations and analyzes its role in genome representation learning.

Using that theoretical analysis, the authors develop a lightweight model for binning at the genome-read level. The model relies only on the fragments’ k-mer compositions. This concentrates the representation on a restricted input description and makes scalability a central part of the method’s design, alongside its ability to support useful grouping.

Comparisons with recent genome foundation models show comparable performance while the proposed model scales substantially better. This matters because practical metagenomic binning requires processing real-world collections of DNA fragments, where the amount of data is a major consideration. The findings support revisiting a relatively simple representation when it offers a favorable combination of task performance and capacity to handle larger datasets.
neurips-2024-revisiting-k-mer-profile-fo.tldr: A lightweight model using only k-mer composition matches recent genome foundation models in reported binning performance while scaling substantially better.

paragraphs: Formal specifications have been proposed as a way to make autonomous-system policies understandable and checkable by people. This paper examines whether people can actually use signal temporal logic, or STL, to validate robot behavior. It builds on earlier findings that presenting formal specifications in different ways did not enable reliable validation even for simple behaviors.

The study tests active learning as a pedagogical intervention intended to improve understanding. Participants encounter one of three conditions: no active learning, active learning, or active learning with feedback. The comparison asks whether engaging people more directly in the learning process helps them judge whether behavior satisfies a specification.

Overall validation accuracy is reported as 65%, with a standard deviation of 15 percentage points. The three conditions do not differ significantly. These results leave the claimed human-interpretability benefit of formal specifications unsupported in this study, and the tested teaching interventions do not establish an improvement. The paper points toward further development of approaches that could make human validation more effective.
neurips-2024-stl-still-tricky-logic-for-.tldr: Active-learning interventions did not significantly improve people’s ability to validate robot behavior from signal temporal logic specifications.

paragraphs: VideoStreaming addresses the large number of visual tokens produced by long videos. Reducing those tokens through sparse sampling or compression can lose temporal information or spatial detail. The proposed model instead processes a video as a sequence of short clips while carrying forward a compact memory of what has already been seen.

Each clip is encoded together with the preceding clip’s encoded memory, producing a fixed-length representation of the video up to that point. After encoding, an adaptive selection mechanism chooses a constant number of historical memories relevant to the question. Those selected memories are passed to the language model to produce an answer.

Separating video encoding from question answering also allows the system to answer several questions by selecting different stored memories, without encoding the entire video again. Experiments report stronger performance and greater efficiency on long-video benchmarks, including detailed questions requiring temporal understanding. The design keeps the selected video input to the language model bounded while using propagated and historical memories to represent a longer sequence.
neurips-2024-streaming-long-video-unders.tldr: VideoStreaming combines clip-by-clip memory propagation with question-specific memory selection for efficient long-video question answering.

paragraphs: Multi-modal entity alignment identifies corresponding entities across knowledge graphs assembled from different sources. Matching becomes difficult when descriptions vary, some modalities are absent, or different kinds of evidence have weak semantic connections. TMEA addresses these uncertain correspondences directly, complementing the emphasis of earlier work on stronger encoders and feature fusion.

For varied attribute descriptions, the method uses a language model and in-context learning to align and filter attributes, then generates and embeds an abstract representation. For missing modalities, it maps features into a shared latent space and uses variational autoencoders to generate substitute features from the available information. These components address two distinct reasons that corresponding entities may appear dissimilar.

A further mechanism uses cross-attention with orthogonal constraints to strengthen common information across modalities. Experiments on two real-world datasets show clear improvements over competitive baselines. The findings support treating variation, missing information, and weak cross-modal associations as explicit alignment problems, with separate mechanisms for each, rather than relying solely on more complete feature descriptions.
neurips-2024-tackling-uncertain-correspo.tldr: TMEA improves entity alignment by addressing varied descriptions, missing modalities, and weak semantic connections across modalities.

paragraphs: Collecting many experts’ models creates an opportunity to combine complementary knowledge, but also makes useful combinations difficult to find. RHEA addresses this problem by converting diverse expert-created models into equivalent neural networks. It then recombines and refines those networks through a population-based evolutionary search.

The framework is first demonstrated in a formal synthetic domain, where the authors show a transparent and systematic process. It is then applied to submissions from the XPRIZE Pandemic Response Challenge. That challenge involved more than 100 teams across 23 countries, producing models for predicting COVID-19 cases and recommending non-pharmaceutical interventions across 235 geographic jurisdictions.

RHEA recombines and refines the challenge’s 169 policy-suggestion models. Evaluation using real-world data finds a broader and more effective collection of policies than either AI or human experts alone. The findings suggest that AI can help extract additional value from existing human expertise by searching for productive combinations of its contributions. The reported evidence concerns policy evaluation using data, rather than outcomes from deploying those policies.
neurips-2024-unlocking-the-potential-of-.tldr: RHEA recombines expert-created models through evolutionary search, producing broader and more effective policy options in a pandemic-response evaluation.

paragraphs: Gradient boosting builds an ensemble sequentially, fitting each new weak learner to a signal describing how the current prediction should change. This paper extends that procedure to supervised problems whose target values are probability distributions. The desired prediction is therefore itself a distribution associated with an input.

The proposed Wasserstein gradient boosting changes the correction signal used at each iteration. New weak learners fit Wasserstein gradients of loss functionals defined over probability distributions. This supplies a distribution-oriented counterpart to ordinary boosting’s pseudo residuals, allowing the sequential ensemble procedure to optimize predictions in this different output space.

A main application is tree-based evidential learning. Here the model returns a distribution over a response parameter, expressing uncertainty about that parameter instead of supplying only its point estimate. The authors empirically compare the resulting probabilistic predictions with existing uncertainty-quantification methods and report competitive performance. The contribution connects the familiar boosting framework to learning tasks where representing uncertainty in the output parameter is a central objective.
neurips-2024-wasserstein-gradient-boosti.tldr: Wasserstein gradient boosting extends sequential ensemble learning to distribution-valued predictions and shows competitive uncertainty-quantification performance.
